_comment: OUTWARD-EFFECT DISPOSITIONS for the order-issue domain (RI-ORDERS / O4-ISSUE).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Shadow mode snapshots state, runs the original, RESTORES the pre-state,
runs ours, and compares. Restoring state does not un-play a sound. So an outward call with an
external effect fires TWICE per armed call while the state comparison still reads clean. This
file is the authored half of the answer -- the INVENTORY is measured
(`gen_migration.py --domain orders_issue --effects`), the DISPOSITION is a judgement.
THE SURFACE HERE IS ONE TARGET, which is the whole point of an order-issue wrapper: it packs a
command and hands it to the container. Two of the 112 talk to anything irreversible, and both
`verified: true` is inherited, not re-asserted: this is the SAME target the sim domain already
confirmed against its body (tools/data/sim_effect_classes.json), at the same evidence address.
Two domains calling one function do not need two readings of it -- but if that entry is ever
revised, revise this one with it.

llm_snd_play.why: Device write. Reaches llm_snd_play_matching_sample on BOTH paths (CALL 0x004d2b44 @0x00425368 and @0x00425408) -> llm_snd_channel_configure_voice_and_play @0x004e14c0, and writes per-channel priority (@0x0042537b) and current-sound-id (@0x00425388) unconditionally on the play path. Read against the body for the sim domain; the same reading holds here. Its two callers in this domain are the order-acknowledgement voice line (llm_strat_group_order_ack_voice) and the move-with-bump confirmation (llm_strat_unit_order_move_confirmed_with_bump) -- so an unseamed shadow arm would double every order-ack chirp the player hears.
